pos.personaBrief: Bayern dominated possession against low blocks (Coaches' Voice Dusseldorf, Leverkusen final) and theScore says the system dominates rather than nullifies; yet they gladly gave the ball back in the final and Barcelona game to counter.

pro.personaBrief: Quick forward play after regains (3 of 4 goals within 10s vs Barca, early forward passes), yet ball-playing centre-backs, Neuer and Kimmich/Thiago dropping show build-up from the back against the press.

est.personaBrief: Coaches' Voice describes constant attacker rotations and vertical rotations of the midfielders; Flick's side is fluid rather than zone-fixed, with a roaming Muller and Lewandowski, and wide players moving into half-spaces.

lar.personaBrief: Width came from athletic full-backs Davies and Pavard overlapping while Coman and Gnabry drifted into half-spaces; crosses into the middle against Barca; central Lewandowski/Muller remained the finishers.

blo.personaBrief: Highest line in the big five, aggressive gegenpressing, front five hounding the build-up (StatsBomb, BFW), proactive defending.

mar.personaBrief: Evidence is thin: open-play pressing almost man to man (360Player, tier C) but also collective space-based high-line defending and corner offside squeeze; no dedicated star-marker evidenced.

pla.personaBrief: Own pressing and high-line identity kept against all opponents (PSG, Barca), with tailored details such as the three-man line vs PSG and Kimmich's role; Flick stated a defined plan each game and adapted to players on arrival.

res.personaBrief: Flick wants intensity and attractive possession football while winning everything; the team kept attacking (8-2) and he showed no sign of parking the bus.

sis.personaBrief: Strong collective system (everyone presses, Goretzka: a tactical plan for every game) with defined roles, though stars like Lewandowski and Muller thrive within it.

jog.personaBrief: Pace and intensity (Davies, Alaba, Goretzka) underpin the high line and press, combined with technical passers like Kimmich and Thiago.

bas.personaBrief: A veteran-core squad of expensive signings (Lewandowski, Neuer, Boateng, Thiago), with Davies and Alaba-type trust in a few youngsters but not a youth-first project.

lid.personaBrief: Flick created a tight, happy dressing room (theScore, Goretzka) and managed people like Muller, while Neuer as right-hand man; tactical authority stayed with him and rules applied to all.
